claims.text: NiCoCrAlTi is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The solution-treated or as-sintered NiCoCrAlTi reference alloy has a predominantly single-phase microstructure.
Aging NiCoCrAlTi at 750–850 °C for an optimized duration will precipitate nanoscale L12-type particles.
The L12 precipitates produced by the proposed treatment will be metastable rather than fully stabilized.
Controlled low- or intermediate-temperature aging can produce a fine, high-density, uniformly dispersed population of L12 particles.
An inert aging atmosphere will prevent oxidation and help preserve the desired nanoscale precipitate dispersion.
At room temperature, applied mechanical load will induce a phase transformation in the metastable L12 precipitates.
Stress-induced transformation of the L12 precipitates will absorb deformation energy.
Transformation-induced plasticity of the L12 precipitates will increase strain hardening and maintain or improve ductility.
Fine L12 precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
Nanoscale intragranular L12 precipitates can provide strengthening without an excessive loss of plasticity.
Relative to a non-aged or homogenized single-phase reference, the aged alloy will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the reference alloy, the aged alloy will exhibit improved strain hardening and an enhanced overall strength–ductility combination.
Over-aging or under-aging may prevent the proposed precipitation-strengthening and TRIP synergy.
Testing at temperatures substantially different from room temperature may suppress the expected TRIP effect.
Small changes in alloy composition may alter the transformation kinetics and the balance between precipitate stability and transformation propensity.
